======================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RAJIV ROY  ORAL ORDER 5 07-01-2025 Heard the parties.
opennyai_summary.7_January_2025__decision:
2. The present petition has been preferred for quashing the order taking cognizance dated 03.02.2022 against the petitioners and others by learned Judicial Magistrate 2 nd class, Begusarai in connection with Complaint Case No. 1604(c)/2021 under Section 323, 406 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. Since the opposite party no. 2 has already appeared, with the consent of the parties, let the matter go before the Mediation Center where the parties shall remain present on 16.01.2025 and a report be submitted to the Court on 17.02.2025.
4.
5. The petitioner shall be paying Rs. 5,000/- as a conveyance charge to the lady on the day she will visit the Mediation Center.
opennyai_summary.arguments: This order has been passed in the background of the fact that it is the categorical statement of the learned counsel for the petitioner that they want an amicable settlement and further, wants to welcome the lady to their house with full dignity and honour.
opennyai_summary.final__PREAMBLE:
Raj Kishore Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 1 December, 2025
1
 In The Supreme Court Of India

 Criminal Appeal No. /2025
[@ Slp [Crl.] No.15579/2023]
 Raj Kishore Singh Appellant(s)
 Versus
 The State Of Bihar & Anr. Respondent(s)
 O R D E R
Leave granted.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The appellant has been arrayed as accused No.2 in CC No.695/2021 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The appellant is the father-in-law of respondent No.2 being the complainant.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Upon perusal of the same, we find absolutely no material to implicate the appellant for the aforementioned offences.
The statements made on oath by the complainant and the witnesses are an improved version of the complaint which, in our considered view, cannot be taken note of.
We are of the view that the decision rendered by this Court in Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam & Ors.
v. State of Bihar & Ors. reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599, as relied upon by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant would apply to the facts of the present case.
Suffice it is to state that continuing the criminal proceedings against the appellant would amount to harassment and a travesty of justice.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Accordingly, the impugned order is set aside and consequently, the proceedings arising out of CC No. 695/2021 stand quashed qua the appellant.
The appeal stands allowed, accordingly.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
The appeal stands allowed in terms of the signed order.
